ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 70:30 ratio of high-intensity (white/light-grey) to low-intensity (black/dark-grey) pixels across the visible ventral surface.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-intensity contiguous white fields dominate the central-medial regions of both lobes. Low-intensity pixels are mapped as a continuous border along the trailing edge and concentrated at the distal tips. A dense field of high-contrast, dark-grey circular blobs is mapped to the mid-distal quadrant of the right lobe, with smaller, sparse clusters mapped to the medial region of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous high-frequency serration along the trailing edge with pixel amplitudes ranging from approximately 4 to 12 pixels. The serration pattern is irregular, with deeper indentations visible near the mid-sections of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge exhibits a macro-level convex sweep from the medial section towards the distal tips, terminating in a sharp upward curvature at the distal-most points.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Highly distinct constellations of dark-grey circular pixel clusters (rosettes) are localized on the right lobe. Dense, irregular dark textured pixel masses are visible at the extreme distal tips of both lobes, corresponding to external colonization.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: A series of roughly parallel, faint vertical linear pixel disruptions (rake-like marks) are visible on the interior-medial portion of the left lobe, cutting through the primary white pigmentation.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Prominent irregular growth and darkening at the distal tips of both lobes indicating heavy barnacle colonization and associated tissue alteration.
other_distinctive_markers: The right lobe features a unique, high-contrast 'leopard-spot' pigmentation pattern that is absent from the left lobe.
